replaces: the shell agent monitor: lib/mentiko-monitor.sh + lib/monitor-completion.sh + the monitor-side helpers in lib/agent-functions.sh (monitor-agent-died, stale/nudge, latch)
preserves: docs/orchestration/contracts/monitor.contract.json is the v1 behavior of record; every invariant and behavior there must survive the port unchanged unless explicitly superseded below

flag.name: MENTIKO_MONITOR_V2
flag.scope: typed agent monitor loop; independent of MENTIKO_RUNNER_V2 (typed launch) and MENTIKO_RUNNER_V2_COMPLETION (typed completion verdict)

why.problem: the monitor — the loop that watches an agent over time and owns the patient 'wait, nudge, then latch' behavior — is still shell, while the completion verdict (a one-shot) is typed. The shell monitor is PATIENT: it nudges a stalled-but-alive agent and only latches completion on a real declared event or a standalone AGENT_COMPLETE. But the typed completion bridge it invokes runs its OWN blind retry/exhaust with no view of liveness. That split-brain — patient shell watcher, impatient typed verdict — is exactly what failed TASK-093: the typed bridge exhausted and declared the agent failed while the agent was still alive and emitted its declared event ~4.5 minutes later.
why.fix: unify the watch loop and the completion verdict under ONE typed owner that shares a single liveness view. Once the monitor is typed, completion is invoked ONLY when the agent is genuinely done (latched event / AGENT_COMPLETE / dead-with-event), never speculatively while the agent is alive and eventless. There is then no blind exhaustion to make. The false-failure guards in runner-v2-contract.json (completion_liveness_contract: liveness_wins, bounded_await, late_event_recovery) become structurally enforced by the owner that actually observes liveness, instead of being built-but-unfed as they are today.
why.deletion_gate: the shell monitor scripts MUST NOT be deleted until this typed monitor reaches proven parity (every invariant below) and MENTIKO_MONITOR_V2 defaults on. Deleting them earlier removes agent monitoring entirely — nothing else watches sessions, latches completion, or re-triggers the verdict.

spawn.current: web/lib/runner-v2/agent-bootstrap-plan.ts buildMonitorCommand builds the shell monitor command (lib/mentiko-monitor.sh); the typed bootstrap spawns it as the monitor PTY. So even a typed launch monitors via shell today.
spawn.v2: buildMonitorCommand emits a typed monitor command (compiled node monitor-v2 entry, <session> <chain.json>) when MENTIKO_MONITOR_V2 is enabled; identical PTY-spawn contract, identical env carry, identical singleton semantics
spawn.fallback: shell mentiko-monitor.sh when the flag is off, or when the typed monitor exits unsupported before it has latched or handled anything (mirror the runner/completion exit-64 fallback discipline: no fallback after the typed monitor has mutated latch/nudge/run state)

entrypoints.env_carry: the pty daemon whitelists spawn env, so the typed monitor command must inline-export the same context the shell monitor carries (monitor.contract.json launches.completion_env): MENTIKO_RUN_DIR/RUNS_DIR, EVENTS_DIR, STATE_DIR, NAMESPACE_ID/ORG_ID, MENTIKO_CODE_ROOT anchored from the engine location, and both runner-v2 flags — otherwise the completion it launches cannot resolve run context.

monitor_loop.watch: poll the session capture on an interval (shell: lib/mentiko-monitor.sh while-loop with CHECK_INTERVAL); the typed port keeps the same poll-until-terminal shape and must NOT block or run inside the completion PTY
monitor_loop.completion_latch: OR-latch (monitor.contract.json completion_latch): a standalone AGENT_COMPLETE line on its own stripped terminal line, OR a declared emits event whose source contains the agent id and whose run id matches. Latch recorded at ~/.mentiko_monitor/${session}_complete.
monitor_loop.stale: md5 of the last 20 captured lines unchanged marks a stale tick (advisor_threshold MENTIKO_ADVISOR_STALE_COUNT default 3, max_stale default 5). Stale drives advisor nudges / blocked diagnostics ONLY — never completion. 'stale output does not imply completion.'
monitor_loop.nudge_budget: durable ceiling MENTIKO_MONITOR_MAX_NUDGES tracked in ~/.mentiko_monitor/${session}_nudges; survives screen-echo stale resets and monitor restarts; an exhausted budget escalates (awaits latch) instead of nudging forever (20ce3b1). The typed port MUST persist this to disk, not memory, or a monitor restart resets the budget.
monitor_loop.death: local workspaces: pgrep the child process under the pane pid. remote (ssh/docker): SKIP local process-death checks. Death classification is EVENT-FIRST: process gone WITH a genuine completion event -> complete normally; process gone WITHOUT an event -> failed diagnostic agent-error (agent-functions.sh monitor-agent-died).
monitor_loop.liveness_wins: an agent whose session is alive and still producing output is NEVER classified dead or failed for a missing event; the loop keeps watching and nudging within budget. This is the structural form of runner-v2-contract.json completion_liveness_contract.liveness_wins — enforced here by the component that actually observes liveness.

completion_handoff.invoke: the monitor launches the completion verdict in a SEPARATE pty (never the monitor pty), and ONLY on a genuine latch (event / AGENT_COMPLETE) or on death-with-event — never speculatively while the agent is alive and eventless
completion_handoff.shared_liveness: because the typed monitor already holds the liveness view, it either (a) passes that view into the typed completion verdict, or (b) simply does not invoke completion until the agent is genuinely done. Either way the typed completion's blind retry/exhaust — the root of TASK-093 — is removed. This is where completion-runner.ts evaluateAgentLiveness/await-liveness finally receives a real signal from its true owner.
completion_handoff.one_owner: exactly one owner applies completion side effects. In the fully-typed path there is NO shell completion fallback; the typed monitor + typed completion are the single owner. Until parity, the exit-64 shell completion fallback remains (monitor.contract.json launches.typed_bridge: completion pty runs node runner-v2-complete first, exit != 64 terminal, exit 64 execs the shell completion script).
completion_handoff.no_blind_exhaustion: the migrated path MUST NOT contain a completion verdict that terminalizes an agent for a missing event without the monitor's liveness view. Blind exhaustion is the specific defect being removed; a parity test must prove a stalled-but-alive agent is never failed.

disk_contracts.capture_source: the pty session capture (transport capture) the shell monitor md5s; AGENT_COMPLETE is resolved against the DURABLE session transcript JSONL (by session UUID), never the re-wrappable rendered screen (BUG-022 durable-evidence latch), so a resized instruction echo cannot false-latch

parity_requirements: md5-of-last-20-lines stale detection reproduced, or a proven-equivalent change detector that never regresses 'stale is not complete'
durable nudge budget persisted to disk, surviving screen-echo stale resets and monitor restarts
AGENT_COMPLETE latch requires a standalone marker in the DURABLE transcript JSONL, never the rendered screen (BUG-022)
event match respects agent id (source superstring) and run id
death classification is event-first, and skips local process-death checks for ssh/docker workspaces
completion handler runs in a separate pty, never the monitor pty
singleton/daemon spawn semantics and full env carry preserved
invariants: dead without declared event is not success
completion matcher never accepts monitor diagnostic events
AGENT_COMPLETE must be a standalone durable-transcript line (BUG-022)
event match respects agent id and run id
completion handler runs outside the monitor pty
screen-echo repaints never grant more nudges: the nudge budget is durable (20ce3b1)
liveness wins: never classify an alive, producing agent as dead or failed for a missing event
death is event-first: process gone WITH a completion event completes normally
the monitor is the re-check loop: completion is invoked only when genuinely done, so no verdict makes a blind, liveness-unaware exhaustion decision (the TASK-093 fix)
do not delete the shell monitor until typed parity is proven and MENTIKO_MONITOR_V2 defaults on
known_gaps: the typed completion bridge (completion-runner.ts) already contains a liveness-aware await path (evaluateAgentLiveness / await-liveness) and a late-event recovery (recoverLateCompletionEvents) that are BUILT BUT UNFED/UNWIRED (runner-v2-contract.json known_gaps). Once the typed monitor owns liveness, decide deliberately: FEED them (monitor passes liveness into completion) or REMOVE them as redundant (monitor gates invocation on genuine-done). Do not leave both a gating monitor and a dead await path.

the shell md5-of-20-lines detector is heuristic and known-blind to spinner redraws (agent-functions.sh comment); the port should preserve behavior but may improve the change detector without weakening 'stale is not complete'
remote (ssh/docker) liveness has no local pid to pgrep; the typed monitor must reproduce the shell remote-skip and lean on event/transcript evidence for those workspaces
the monitor is a long-lived per-agent PTY loop, not a one-shot; the typed port must handle its own restart/idempotency (durable latch + nudge files) the way the shell monitor does
migration_plan: 2. typed monitor loop behind MENTIKO_MONITOR_V2 (default off): watch + latch + stale + durable nudge + event-first death, at parity with the shell monitor, with NO completion-handoff changes yet
3. wire buildMonitorCommand to emit the typed monitor command when the flag is on; keep shell fallback and full env carry
4. unify the completion handoff: the typed monitor invokes the typed completion verdict with a shared liveness view (or gates invocation on genuine-done); remove the blind exhaustion path
5. parity tests cover every invariant; a runtime proof on a real stalled-but-alive agent (the TASK-093 shape) shows the agent is nudged/awaited and never falsely failed
6. default MENTIKO_MONITOR_V2 on; only THEN delete lib/mentiko-monitor.sh, lib/monitor-completion.sh, and the monitor-side helpers in lib/agent-functions.sh
